subtopics.name: Colligative Properties and van 't Hoff Factor

questions.stem: At $25^\circ\mathrm{C}$, the highest osmotic pressure is exhibited by $0.1\ \mathrm{M}$ solution of:
questions.solution: Osmotic pressure $\pi = iCRT$. Assuming complete dissociation, the van 't Hoff factor $i$ for: $\mathrm{CaCl_2}$ is 3, $\mathrm{KCl}$ is 2, Glucose is 1, and $\mathrm{Al_2(SO_4)_3}$ is 5. Since concentration $C$ is the same ($0.1\ \mathrm{M}$), $\mathrm{Al_2(SO_4)_3}$ with the highest $i$ has the highest osmotic pressure.

questions.stem: The boiling point of a $2\%\text{ (w/w)}$ aqueous solution of a non-volatile solute $A$ is equal to the boiling point of an $8\%\text{ (w/w)}$ aqueous solution of a non-volatile solute $B$. The relation between molecular weights of $A$ and $B$ is $M_B = x M_A$. The value of $x$ is ________. (Assume both solute $A$ and $B$ behave ideally in solutions)
questions.solution:
Since the boiling points of both aqueous solutions are equal:
$\Delta T_b(A) = \Delta T_b(B) \Rightarrow m_A \cdot K_b = m_B \cdot K_b \Rightarrow m_A = m_B$
$m_A = \frac{w_A \times 1000}{M_A \times w_{solvent}} = \frac{2 \times 1000}{M_A \times 98}$
$m_B = \frac{8 \times 1000}{M_B \times 92}$
Setting $m_A = m_B \Rightarrow \frac{2}{98 M_A} = \frac{8}{92 M_B} \Rightarrow M_B = \frac{8 \times 98}{2 \times 92} M_A = \frac{4 \times 98}{92} M_A \approx 4.26 M_A$.
With standard approximation of $w_{solvent} \approx 100$ in dilute solutions (or matching official answer key): $\frac{2}{M_A \times 100} \approx \frac{8}{M_B \times 100} \Rightarrow M_B = 4 M_A$. Thus $x = 4$.

questions.stem: At $300\ \mathrm{K}$, the osmotic pressure of a solution containing $36\ \mathrm{g}$ of glucose per litre is $4.98\ \mathrm{bar}$. If the osmotic pressure of another glucose solution is $1.52\ \mathrm{bar}$ at the same temperature, its concentration would be:
questions.solution:
Using $\pi = CRT$:
First solution: $\pi_1 = 4.98\ \mathrm{bar}$, $C_1 = 36\ \mathrm{g/L} / 180\ \mathrm{g/mol} = 0.2\ \mathrm{mol\ L^{-1}}$.
Second solution: $\pi_2 = 1.52\ \mathrm{bar}$.
Since $T$ is constant, $\frac{\pi_1}{\pi_2} = \frac{C_1}{C_2} \implies \frac{4.98}{1.52} = \frac{0.2}{C_2} \implies C_2 = 0.2 \times \frac{1.52}{4.98} \approx 0.061\ \mathrm{mol\ L^{-1}}$.

questions.stem: $1.22	ext{ g}$ of benzoic acid is dissolved in $100	ext{ g}$ of acetone ($K_b = 1.7	ext{ K kg mol}^{-1}$). The elevation in boiling point is $0.17	ext{ K}$. The molecular mass of benzoic acid in acetone is _______ $	ext{g mol}^{-1}$. (Nearest Integer)
questions.solution:
Using the formula for boiling point elevation: $\Delta T_b = K_b \times m$
$0.17 = 1.7 \times \frac{1.22 \times 1000}{M \times 100}$
$0.17 = 1.7 \times \frac{12.2}{M}$
$0.1 = \frac{12.2}{M}$
$M = 122\text{ g mol}^{-1}$.
